name: Vampire Disko At Valhalla: Goth, Wave, Cult Hits + Vampire Attire
long_description:
Vampire Disko At Valhalla: Goth, Wave, Cult Hits + Vampire Attire

VAMPIRE DISKO: GOTH, WAVE, CULT HITS + VAMPIRE ATTIRE

For one evening only, Wellington descends into darkness as vampyres (don't worry, vampires aren't real...or are they?), goths, and nocturnal misfits gather on the dance floor for the city's first ever VAMPIRE DISKO

Wellington's newest night of Goth, Post-Punk, EBM, Dark Synth Pop, Post Punk, Industrial and Wave for creatures of the night who enjoy getting dressed as vampires, or at least being around people that do!

We invite you to arrive dressed for the eternal night inspired by cult classic vampire films such as Interview with the Vampire, Queen of the Damned, The Lost Boys, The Hunger, Nosteratu and sooo many more... The more dramatic your look, the better! Victorian, Modern, or Halloween Vampire- your efforts will not go unnoticed!

MUSIC IS DECIDEDLY DARK: Expect DJs playing a large amount of 80s classic goth like Bauhaus, Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, Christian Death, Clan of Xymox, Skinny Puppy, Nitzer Ebb, Front 242, classic dark 80s like Depeche Mode, Soft Cell, The Cure, Echo and the Bunnymen and New Order and many cutting edge brank, new artists who lean toward the dark side. Think She Past Away, Boy Harsher, Riki, Kontravoid, Lebanon Hanover, Nox Novacula, H.Ä.L.T., The Frozen Autumn, Patriarchy....

And for those of who you want a taste of 90s-10s, we won't completely shy away, but you simply MUST request a song in the facebook event if you really have your heart set on something.

Soundtracking the night: DJ Matai, Nightmare + more, spinning until the early hours. We DO of course plan to have you in bed before SUNLIGHT HITS!

This is a LGBTQIA+ friendly event where self-expression is encouraged and the dance floor belongs to everyone.

Sharpen your fangs. Dress to kill. Join us for Wellington's most exciting night of the year!

The first Vampire Disko begins on Friday, September 25th

See you after darkness falls

Presale tickets are limited. Get yours before they sell out!

id: Apertures | Alter Natural | Juniper May-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Apertures | Alter Natural | Juniper May
long_description:
Apertures is the duo of Iulia Boșcu (Romania) and Will Gresson (Aotearoa New Zealand). Together they perform dense ambient/drone soundscapes, incorporating field recordings to situate their music into real spaces and lived experience. Outside of Apertures the pair have been active since 2016, working across multiple disciplines involving visual art, publishing and sound with a focus on climate and environmental tensions. Their sound installation work has been shown at Audio Foundation, Te Tuhi (Tāmaki Makaurau), Nine Fathom Deep (Te Whanganui-a-Tara), Sluice (London/Seyðisfjörður) and MATCA (Cluj-Napoca). An archive of their work is available at withoutappeal.org.
-
Alter Natural (aka Nathan Carter of The Temple) is a sound, music, and multi-media artist who strives to immerse the audience in feelings of the sublime – beauty, immensity, drama, wonder, intrigue, mystery, tranquility, joy. In his music, this takes the form of cathartic soundscapes, propulsive EDM grooves, and visually inspired sound design. https://www.alternatural.nz/
-
Juniper May is the solo project of Pōneke artist Lora May. Using an SP-404, she channels and transfigures samples of found sounds, synths and field recordings into melodic, distant and estranged pop songs.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

id: Floyd Marsden - Good Times (with Support From Julia Belle)-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Floyd Marsden - Good Times (with Support From Julia Belle)
long_description:
After a particularly chaotic eight months since her third album release back in January, Floyd Marsden brings a brand new show to The Undercurrent: Good Times. Packed with acoustic jazz-pop songs, stories, and laughs, the show features brand new material written over the last few months (including her newest single So Picturesque), fan favourite tracks, rarely-played deep cuts from her three studio albums, and some special musical guests.

Opening the night is the incredible Julia Belle, a singer-songwriter based in Pōneke Wellington, whose music blends intimate folk songwriting with an evolving indie-pop sound. Known for her emotionally candid lyrics and atmospheric melodies, she explores themes of mental health, OCD, anxiety, escapism, love, loss, and the complexities of navigating your twenties.

Doors open at 8.00pm, with music from 8.30pm.

id: INTRODUCING - indifferent ANiMALS-Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: INTRODUCING - indifferent ANiMALS
long_description:
INTRODUCING…
indifferent ANiMALS
With support from
TestPot
And Zoe Scott and the Sisters

Join us for the first live appearance of the 90's pop rock inspired 4 piece, indifferent ANiMALS.
It's that band Jim, but not as you know it. All new original songs written and performed by each member of the band.
Supporting them is the alt rock trio, TestPot.
After a long winter off, TestPot are back and will be performing some new material for the first time.
Zoe Scott and the Sisters will also be on stage with their blend of cinematic soundscapes and indie folk.
A packed night of original, eclectic music from three great Wellington bands.

—————— x X x ——————

indifferent ANiMALS
The recipe for an Indifferent Animal: take the beating heart of a Bitter Brother, a Gracious Deviant, the blood of a Panther named Agatha, and add a Testpot of Soda.
Four voices. Jangly guitars. Angst, restraint and melody in roughly equal measure.
You thought you'd heard everything – and maybe you have. Indifferent Animals make original music that feels hauntingly familiar: the best bits of 90s indie and Britpop, dragged three decades forward and made new again. Beautiful, melodic, occasionally noisy, and considerably less indifferent than the name suggests.

TestPot
The three piece multi instrumental alt art rock band are back!
After a long winter away, what started as a side project has matured into a collaborative creative view of humanity. TestPot explores subjects around the human condition, invasive surveillance, social media and an unshakable hope in humanity, amongst others.
Musically inspired by bands such as Duran Duran, Leaders as Animals and The Smile.
Experience the sonic and visual exploration into the world of the sell-out Wellington band, back with new material and a never-wavering hope in humankind.

Zoe Scott and the Sisters
A warm blend of indie folk and cinematic soundscapes supports the haunting vocals of Zoe Scott. Performing songs from the new album Homecoming, an atmospheric journey into the intoxicating world of feminist folk pop.

id: Kita: Indie Filmtronica with Remixed Film-San Fran, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Kita: Indie Filmtronica with Remixed Film
long_description:
Front-woman Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant is amidst her Artist in Residence at The Hannah Theatre in Wellington, translating her debut art-house film LOVE LIVES HERE 愛住在這裡 for stage. The narrative originally inspired by the band's EP LOVE LIVES HERE which they toured nationwide in 2023. Tu-Bryant is debuting the film into a full immersive cinema-live-theatrical experience with a chorus of dancers and live band for her residency at the end of this year. In the meantime, she revives the live-in-concert version of this vulnerable ambitious work-in-progress. Excerpts from the film will be remixed live by Elfling. This show was showcased at Twisted Frequency, and now powerhouse trio KITA bring it back to the capital playing one of their favourite venues in Pōneke, SANFRAN.
Recent Aotearoa #1 HINE aka GiGi Crayford will be warming the space,m playing support.
Expect Punctual Start - you don't want to miss the beginning.

KITA
Melding inspirations of folk, soul, pop and psychedelia with the guitar and spirited storytelling of musician-actor Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant (Avatar 2, Far North); the thick lushness of Moog synth and Fender Rhodes from Ed Zuccollo (aka Zuke); and the filthy drive and barking drums of Rick Cranson (Little Bushman), KITA have long-since solidified themselves as a must-see live band with a massive sound.

Newtown Rocksteady are packing the groove wagon for two September outings: St Peters Hall, Paekākāriki on 25 September, followed by a long overdue return to their roots at the Newtown Community Centre on 26 September for a proper hometown skank.
The band was born in 2007 from a regular open jam at Newtown Community Centre, and they’ve been keeping the neighbourhood moving ever since with their own warm, loose-limbed take on rocksteady, ska and reggae.
There’ll be fresh tunes, old favourites, basslines to move ya waistlines and all of that groovy goodness, so come for the tunes, stay for the dancefloor and leave with a wide grin.
Two nights, one big-hearted band, plenty of good-time vintage reggae energy. Bring your people, bring your dancing shoes, and let Newtown Rocksteady do what they do best!!

Support on both shows from the the most soulful being in wellington... the man... George Young

You can grab tickets from buytickets.at/newtownrocksteady
